page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-1200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 192.0 GB of system memory providing 8.0 GB per core, and 1200 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include a GPU. The CPU features 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache, with support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instruction sets.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench multi-core score, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Single-core performance is also strong in stress-ng, though Geekbench single-core and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average middle 50% range. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, consistently register in the average tier. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also align with average performance tiers.

The server offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1 alongside dedicated CPU allocation and local NVMe storage, presenting a balanced resource density for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without the overhead of GPU acceleration. The combination of strong multi-core processing and local NVMe storage makes this instance suitable for memory-intensive databases, multi-threaded data processing, software compilation, and medium-scale web serving workloads.
